macOS-26 Tahoe is now available for all GitHub Actions, and you can use the macos-26 image label in your YAML to select this image. ## Available macOS runner labels

| Image | YAML label(s) | Status |

| macOS 26 Arm64 | `macos-latest`, `macos-26`, `macos-26-xlarge` | GA |

Note `macos-latest` now resolves to **macos-26 Arm64** (the rollout completed after June 15, 2026).

## Xcode per image

**macos-26 / macos-latest** — OS 26.4 (25E246), image 20260720.0390.1. Identical Xcode lineup on both Arm64 and Intel variants:

| Version | Build | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **26.6** | 17F113 | no |
| **26.5** | 17F42 | **yes (default)** |
| 26.4.1 | 17E202 | no |
| 26.3 | 17C529 | no |
| 26.2 | 17C52 | no |

| 26.0.1 | 17A400 | no |

SDKs in Xcode 26.6: macOS 26.5, **iOS 26.5** (`iphoneos26.5`), tvOS 26.5, watchOS 26.5, visionOS 26.5, DriverKit 25.5. iOS SDKs present across the image: 26.0, 26.1, 26.2, 26.4, 26.5.

**macos-15** — OS 15.7.7 (24G720). Xcode 26.3, 26.2, 26.1.1, 26.0.1, then 16.4 (**default**, build 16F6), 16.3, 16.2, 16.1, 16.0.

**macos-14** (deprecated) — OS 14.8.7. Tops out at 16.2; default 15.4. No Xcode 26.

**xcode-27** (beta) — OS 26.5.2 (25F84). Single Xcode: **27.0 beta**, build 27A5218g, default, at `/Applications/Xcode_27_beta_3.app`. SDK iOS 27.0.

## Direct answers

**Is Xcode 26.x available? Yes.** On `macos-26` / `macos-latest` / `macos-26-intel` (versions 26.0.1 through **26.6**), and partially on `macos-15` (26.0.1 through 26.3). On macos-26 the default is **26.5, not 26.6** — 26.6 is installed but must be selected explicitly.

**Highest Xcode overall:** 27.0 beta (build 27A5218g) on the `xcode-27` beta image; highest stable is **26.6 (17F113)** on macos-26.

**Your project can build on GitHub Actions — yes.** `CreatedOnToolsVersion = 26.6` matches Xcode 26.6 exactly, and `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.5` is satisfied by the iOS 26.5 SDK that ships in both Xcode 26.5 and 26.6. Use `runs-on: macos-26` and, since 26.6 is not the default, select it explicitly:

```yaml
runs-on: macos-26
steps:
  - run: sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_26.6.app
```

Caveat worth flagging: the readme is a snapshot of the current image build. Because 26.6 is not the default, it is the version most at risk of being rotated out in a future image update — pinning to `Xcode_26.6.app` will hard-fail if that happens. Falling back to the default (26.5) also works for a 26.5 deployment target if you don't strictly need 26.6.

Do **not** use `macos-15` — its newest Xcode is 26.3, whose iOS SDK is below your 26.5 deployment target.
